chapter: Lawn parties, excursions and dance-hall work
title: Toodlum's place on Howard Street
summary: Toodlum (Napoleon Johnson), a pimp and gambler, ran a Sunday-night place where Buddy Petit, Chris Kelly and others played.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Tell us about Toodlum's place. Toodlum, well... Duncan, Sidney Bichet used to talk about him.
And Toodlum, who would play around Toodlum's place a lot was Buddy Petit, Rene, Chris Kelly. Punch. Punch. Punch player? That during time was Punch time. Yeah. It was in Punch time. So...
What sort of fellow was Toodlum? Quiet, nice, fine?
Toodlum? Toodlum was a hustler. One of them big pimps. One of them big pimps, big gamblers.
See, those big old shots there.
Yeah. His right name was Napoleon Johnson.
Yeah. Oh, nice. Wooden Jones told us about that. Remember him, though? Yeah.
He's a big fella, too. Napoleon. Big fella he was. Napoleon Johnson.

Well, did those things just happen occasionally, or was there... Once a week, maybe. Once a week, maybe. Oh, yeah, once a week. I guess it was about all the musicians played there, no? One time or not. Yeah, mostly around on Sunday nights. Yeah, mostly around on Sunday nights. Where was Tumley's place again? It was on Howard. On Howard.
